analysis.title: S&P 500 Futures: Post-Election Chop
key_insights: On November 5th the S&P 500 fell 4.4%. Hyperscalers (-3.4%) could no longer offset Semiconductors (-12.2%), which fell on lower expectations for datacenter buildout.
S&P futures aggregate open interest rose $19.1bn on November 5th, the 5th largest 1-day jump in the past 2 years excluding roll periods. This indicates significant short selling via futures.

From November 5th to 9th the S&P recovered 2.7% and aggregate open interest fell $16.6bn. Stabilization in AI and a drop in oil on improving prospects for an end to the Iran-US War forced quick short covering, even though the S&P did not reach its prior level.
S&P 3-month funding cheapened throughout the whole price chop. GS suggests dealers likely regained arbitrage capacity after leveraged ETF exposure unwound, and that trend followers liquidated.
Short and medium-term momentum signals flipped on the GS Futures Strategists' CTA framework. This partly offset the reduction in downside exposure.

On the morning of November 10th, Waller supported a December hike and opened the door to a half-percentage-point increase. US 10-year real yields rose despite a continued decline in Brent. S&P E-Mini traded -11bps versus settle.

GS argues the fate of Semiconductors arguably still carries more weight than real yields. Asset Manager S&P 500 shorts remained negatively correlated to Semiconductors as of the last Commitment of Traders update, while the historically positive relationship with 10-year real yields was weaker.
